title: Channel models for wearable and implantable WBANs (IEEE P802.15-08-0416-04-0006)
what_they_did: Measured body-surface (CM3) and body-to-external (CM4) propagation from 400 MHz to 2.4 GHz and UWB in a hospital room and in an anechoic chamber, then fitted log-distance path-loss models with a log-normal stochastic term for each band.
useful_for_us: Direct on-body 2.4 GHz model: anechoic PL = 29.3*log10(d_mm) - 16.8 with sigma 6.89 dB, hospital room PL = 6.60*log10(d_mm) + 36.1 with sigma 3.80 dB; body presence adds up to 25 dB anechoic and under 10 dB in a room, and CM4 back-side body shadowing is about 20 dB.

title: A Statistical Model for Shadowed Body-Centric Communications Channels: Theory and Validation
what_they_did: Derived and validated a lognormal-shadowed fading pdf for body-centric links, then fitted it to 2.45 GHz anechoic-chamber measurements of walking on-body links (front-left-waist to right-head, right-knee, right-wrist) and to off-body links during a 360 degree user rotation at 1.5 m and 4 m.
useful_for_us: Shows the fading law our link sees when the wearer walks: a shadowed dominant component persists on every on-body link, the wrist link has the widest spread, and body rotation produces the worst-case off-body fades we must design the 99th percentile around.

title: NINA-B3 series data sheet UBX-17052099 (NINA-B306)
what_they_did: Vendor data sheet for the NINA-B3 Bluetooth 5.0 module family, listing conducted output power, EIRP, receiver sensitivity for 1 Mbit/s and long-range (Coded) modes, supported data rates and current consumption for the NINA-B301/B302/B306 variants.
useful_for_us: Our radio's numbers: NINA-B306 typical conducted output +8 dBm, EIRP +10 dBm, RX sensitivity -94 dBm for 1 Mbit/s and -100 dBm in long-range Coded mode; it is the TX and RX row of the link budget.

title: u-blox NINA-B30 series (open CPU) product page
what_they_did: Vendor product page for the NINA-B30 modules that confirms the chip inside, antenna options, maximum EIRP and throughput, and that LE 2M and Coded PHY are supported on the NINA-B306.
useful_for_us: Confirms the NINA-B306 carries an nRF52840, has an internal PCB antenna, 10 dBm EIRP, 1.4 Mbit/s maximum throughput and supports both the 2M and long-range Coded PHYs, which fixes our PHY options.

title: BLE very weak signal (Arduino Nano 33 BLE forum thread)
what_they_did: Arduino Nano 33 BLE owners compared BLE range with nRF Connect and BLE Scanner on phones and laptops, then traced the short range of several boards to two missing components in the NINA-B306 antenna matching network.
useful_for_us: Real NINA-B306 (Arduino Nano 33 BLE) field numbers: units with missing matching parts are detected under 2 m and reliable at about 1 m, a good unit reached 40 m line-of-sight outdoors and about 4-5 m elsewhere, which shows the range spread is dominated by the module's antenna matching.

title: Distance bluetooth range Arduino Nano 33 BLE (Arduino forum thread)
what_they_did: A Nano 33 BLE user measured how far the board's BLE advertisements were received by a laptop's internal Bluetooth card, by a phone and by a plug-in USB Bluetooth adapter, and reported each distance.
useful_for_us: Shows the phone/laptop radio, not the pod, can be the weak link: 45-50 cm to a built-in laptop card, more than 5 m to a phone, and 7-8 m after switching to a USB adapter, so we must test with the actual phones.

title: List of Coded PHY supported/tested phones (nordicsemi/Android-BLE-Library issue #166)
what_they_did: Nordic engineers and Android developers collected hands-on tests of which phones can scan and connect using the LE Coded PHY as the primary advertising PHY, including failures, over four years of reports.
useful_for_us: Lists the phones that actually work with long-range Coded advertising (Galaxy S10 and newer, S21, Tab A7, OnePlus 7 and newer, Poco X3 NFC, Samsung M51) and the ones that fail (Pixel, Galaxy A32 5G), so we know Coded PHY cannot be assumed on all phones.

title: Bluetooth LE performance: receiver characteristics (BDE-BW3551P1)
what_they_did: Vendor data sheet page listing measured Bluetooth LE receiver sensitivity for one modern combo module at 125 kbit/s Coded, 500 kbit/s Coded, 1 Mbit/s and 2 Mbit/s at a 30.2 percent PER.
useful_for_us: A current-phone-class radio floor: -104 dBm at 125 kbit/s Coded (S=8), -101.4 dBm at 500 kbit/s Coded (S=2), -97.5 dBm at 1 Mbit/s (37-byte) and -95.4 dBm at 2 Mbit/s, giving the phone RX row for the link budget.

title: A Link Loss Model for the On-body Propagation Channel for Binaural Hearing Aids
what_they_did: Simulated and measured the 2.45 GHz ear-to-ear creeping-wave channel on heterogeneous human phantoms (Duke, Billie) and on a SAM head with 3D-printed pinnae, then fitted an analytical link-loss model.
useful_for_us: Quantifies how much the head blocks a 2.4 GHz link: ear-to-ear link loss is 79 dB on the Duke phantom and 49/64/71/75 dB on SAM as the shell and pinnae become realistic, pinnae add up to 13 dB, head size up to 10 dB, so head shadowing alone can eat most of our budget.

title: Design and Evaluation of a Button Sensor Antenna for On-Body Monitoring Activity in Healthcare Applications
what_they_did: Designed a dual-band textile button antenna, measured S11, gain and radiation efficiency in free space, on the body, bent and after saturating the textile with water, and measured RSSI/path loss in indoor and outdoor LOS and NLOS runs.
useful_for_us: Gives the garment and wet-fabric penalty and an acceptable-loss figure: 72 dB path loss free space and 84 dB worn on the chest/arm, wet fabric shifts S11 and efficiency, and a receiver at -75 dBm tolerates up to 99.4 dB of loss.

title: Link quality estimation and transmit power control for wireless body area networks
what_they_did: Measured packet reception ratio against RSSI, LQI and transmit power on body-worn nodes while walking, and built and evaluated transmit-power-control schemes that keep links above a target quality.
useful_for_us: Ties our radio metrics to reliability: RSSI at or above -90 dBm corresponds to a PRR of 95 percent or more, below -90 dBm variance grows, and the body-area experiment adopts a conservative -85 dBm target, which is exactly the RSSI threshold our firmware should watch.

title: Bluetooth 5 performance analysis for inter-vehicular communications
what_they_did: Ran on-road Bluetooth 5 experiments with LE Coded and 2M PHYs, measuring communication range and application throughput against distance and connection parameters.
useful_for_us: Confirms Coded PHY buys an order of magnitude of range (up to 300 m in their scenario) while application throughput falls as distance grows, which is the range-for-rate trade we will make when the phone is shielded.

title: Bend and Moisture Effects on the Performance of a U-Shaped Slotted Wearable Antenna for Off-Body Communications in an Industrial Scientific Medical (ISM) 2.4 GHz Band
what_they_did: Modelled, built and measured a flexible U-shaped slotted wearable antenna at 2.4 GHz and characterised how bending and moisture loading change its reflection coefficient and radiation performance.
useful_for_us: Backs the wet-fabric and body-loading warnings with a peer-reviewed 2.4 GHz wearable-antenna measurement showing that moisture and bending detune the antenna, so a wet knit hat over the pod is a real loss mechanism, not a cosmetic one.

title: Radio propagation and antenna design for 2.4 GHz wireless harness inside ICT equipment
what_they_did: Measured 2.4 GHz propagation loss inside four metal enclosures, then measured how a commercial chip antenna and a purpose-built shorted microstrip antenna change reflection coefficient as a parallel aluminium plate is brought to 15-60 mm, and measured packet error rate.
useful_for_us: The closest number to our smart-glasses temple problem: a commercial 2.4 GHz chip antenna's S11 degrades to -10 dB at 20-30 mm and -5 dB at 15 mm from a metal plate, while a metal-tolerant design keeps average mismatch loss under 0.4 dB up to 20 mm and reaches PER 1e-5 at about 60 dB of propagation loss.

title: NINA-B3 series system integration manual (UBX-17056748)
what_they_did: Vendor integration manual for the NINA-B3 modules covering the antenna keep-out, ground-plane requirements, EAGP grounding, module placement at a board edge and minimum clearance to the case and to metal parts.
useful_for_us: Sets the layout rules our 10 mm pod cannot fully meet: module at the centre of a board edge, at least 10 mm of ground plane on both sides, no ground under the antenna, the four EAGP pads grounded, and 10 mm clearance to the case and to metal, which is why the design notes already predict reduced range.

title: Bluetooth Core Specification 6.0
what_they_did: The official specification that defines the Bluetooth Low Energy physical layers, including LE 1M, LE 2M and LE Coded with S=2 (500 kbit/s) and S=8 (125 kbit/s), their preamble and coding, and the RF-PHY receiver requirements.
useful_for_us: This is the normative reference for the PHY names and the sensitivity requirement baseline we compare real radios against; it is why Coded S=8 is described as roughly 4x the range of LE 1M and S=2 as the middle step.
